messages.content:
Great — here’s a concrete, user-centered UI domain model for Scenarios that you can review and tune. It maps screens, routes, core components, interactions, and design tokens to your architecture and success criteria.

Information architecture and routes
- Module prefix: /scenarios (mounted within the Risk Shell via Module Federation)
- Primary screens
  - Scenario Inbox (default landing): /scenarios/inbox
  - All Scenarios: /scenarios/all
  - Scenario Details: /scenarios/:scenarioId
    - Summary tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/summary
    - Changes tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/changes
    - Impacts tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/impacts (sub-tabs for FRTB SA and VaR via query ?calc=frtb-sa|var)
    - Approvals tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/approvals
    - Messages tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/messages
    - Audit tab: /scenarios/:scenarioId/audit
  - Global Audit Search: /scenarios/audit
  - Admin: /scenarios/admin
    - Policies: /scenarios/admin/policies
    - Scenario Types: /scenarios/admin/types
    - Reports: /scenarios/admin/reports
- Replace or remap existing screen placeholders
  - Scenario Governance (/governance) → Scenario Inbox (/scenarios/inbox)
  - Scenario Impact Analysis (/analysis-impact) → Scenario Details > Impacts (/scenarios/:scenarioId/impacts)
  - Scenario Admin Configuration (/admin-config) → Admin (/scenarios/admin/*)

Screen blueprints (layout, key components, actions)
1) Scenario Inbox (/scenarios/inbox)
- Goal: What needs my attention now?
- Layout:
  - Header: Title, quick filters (My desk, My approvals due, Status, Scenario Type, Impact severity), Clear filters
  - Toolbar: Search (free text: scenario name, changeSetId), Date range, Columns
  - Grid: Scenario rows with columns: Name, Type, Workflow state, Impact headline delta, Exceptions, Approvals progress (e.g., 1/2), Updated, Owner
  - Right utility panel (collapsible): Selected scenario glance (status, delta, pending approvers), deep links (Market Data change, latest FRTB SA, VaR)
- Primary actions: Open Details, Bulk mark as read (if needed), Refresh
- Empty/error: “No scenarios require attention” with reset filters; error banner with retry

2) All Scenarios (/scenarios/all)
- Goal: Explore full catalog and history
- Similar to Inbox with expanded filter facets (Desk/Book, Data domain, Environment, Promotion status). Add Saved views (per user).

3) Scenario Details (/scenarios/:scenarioId)
- Persistent header:
  - Title + ID, Scenario Type chip, Workflow state badge, Impact headline delta chip, Updated x ago
  - Primary CTA area (contextual): Approve/Reject (if eligible) OR Request Promotion (when approvals satisfied) OR View Promotion Status
  - Secondary actions: Share link, Copy IDs, Open in Market Data, Open FRTB SA, Open VaR
- Context bar:
  - ChangeSet summary: key attrs, totals (direct/indirect), exceptions count
  - Participants: Owner, analysts, approvers (chips with role/status tooltip)
- Tabs and panels:
  - Summary: Cards for Direct Changes (count), Impact Overview (FRTB SA, VaR mini-cards with deltas and links), Approvals Progress (required vs received, SoD flags), Recent Activity (last 5 events)
  - Changes: Data grid from template (columns driven by ScenarioType/ChangeViewDefinition), row details drawer
  - Impacts: Two sub-tabs (FRTB SA, VaR). Each shows:
    - High-level metrics (deltas, distributions if available)
    - “Open full report” link (deep-link into external UIs in shell)
    - Generated Report list (ScenarioImpactReports) with status, timestamp
  - Approvals: Required approvers list (by policy/rule), current decisions, sequence (if any), SoD indicators, RBAC-driven Approve/Reject CTAs
  - Messages: Threaded comments, composer with @mention (optional), timestamps, system event inlines
  - Audit: Immutable event stream for this scenario with filters: event type, user, date. Export if provided later.
- States:
  - Loading skeletons; Poll-driven updates ~5s; “Updated just now” indicator
  - Permissions: Disabled CTAs with tooltip “Your role cannot approve” when RBAC blocks action

4) Global Audit Search (/scenarios/audit)
- Filters: Scenario ID, changeSetId, Event type, User, Date range, Keyword
- Results: Table with Event, Scenario, Actor, Timestamp, Summary. Row expands to payload.

5) Admin (/scenarios/admin/*)
- Policies: List policies, required approver count, priority, enabled flag. Detail drawer shows definition JSON preview.
- Scenario Types: List types with status, icon, behavior flags; manage direct/impact URL templates; preview change view definitions.
- Reports: List report definitions; versions, sample data preview.

Core reusable components
- PageHeader, ContextBar
- StatusBadge (states: Draft, Awaiting Review, Awaiting Approvals, Rejected, Approved, Promotion Requested, Promoted/Failed)
- ImpactDeltaChip (up/down/neutral with magnitude)
- ScenarioGrid (shared table with column presets per type)
- FiltersPanel (facets, saved views)
- ParticipantsChips (with role, decision state)
- ApprovalsProgress (steps, counts, SoD indicators)
- ApprovalCTAs (Approve, Reject) with AttestationModal
- PromotionCTA (Request Promotion) with ConfirmationModal
- MessagesThread and Composer
- AuditEventList and Filters
- ReportTile (FRTB SA, VaR)
- ExternalLinkButton (to Market Data/FRTB SA/VaR with open-in-app icon)
- Toasts/InlineAlerts
- Skeletons: list, cards, detail sections
- EmptyState: headline, description, primary action

Key interactions mapped to endpoints (UI actions)
- Approve scenario
  - Trigger: Click Approve → AttestationModal (comment optional/required by policy) → Confirm
  - Result: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/approve → success toast, update ApprovalsProgress, write AuditEvent
- Reject scenario
  - Trigger: Click Reject → AttestationModal (reason required) → Confirm
  - Result: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/reject → update state to Rejected, toast, audit
- Post message
  - Trigger: Compose → Post
  - Result: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/messages → append to thread, audit
- View impacts
  - Trigger: Open Impacts tab
  - Result: GET /api/scenarios/{id}/impacts; show summary and report links (FRTB SA/VaR)
- Global audit search
  - Trigger: Search
  - Result: GET /api/audit with filters; list results
- Request promotion (when approvals met)
  - Trigger: Request Promotion → ConfirmationModal (target env if applicable) → Confirm
  - Result: UI posts to backend (backend calls Market Data promotions); show “Promotion requested” state; subsequent result arrives via webhook and refresh polling

Navigation and flow patterns
- Primary user tasks
  - Review → from Inbox open Details > Summary/Impacts > add message if needed
  - Approve/Reject → from Details > Approvals, use CTAs; see instant progress update
  - Promote → when eligible, Request Promotion, then track status on Summary
  - Audit → within scenario or via global search
- Micro-frontend deep linking
  - Market Data change detail: open within shell to that module with changeSetId
  - FRTB SA and VaR reports: open within shell; preserve back-stack to Scenario Details
- Real-time updates
  - Poll ~5s; merge-in new messages/approvals; subtle “updated” indicator; manual refresh button for control

Design tokens (baseline, to align with shell)
- Color
  - Primary: #0B5FFF
  - Success/Positive: #1C7C54
  - Warning: #B25E09
  - Danger/Negative: #B00020
  - Neutral 900/700/500/300/100: #1A1A1A/#3C3C3C/#6B6B6B/#B3B3B3/#E6E6E6
  - Impact positive: #0E8A16; Impact negative: #D32F2F; Neutral: #6B6B6B
- Spacing (px): 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32
- Typography
  - Font: system/enterprise standard
  - Sizes (px): 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 28
  - Line-height: 1.4–1.6
- Radii: 4, 8
- Elevation: 0, 2, 4, 8 (focus on low-elevation enterprise feel)
- Border: 1px solid Neutral-300 for cards/panels
- Focus: 2px outline Primary at 3:1 contrast minimum
- Density: Comfortable default; compact option for grids
- Motion: 120–160ms ease-in-out for tabs, drawers, toasts

Accessibility and usability standards
- Contrast: All text ≥ AA; colored deltas accompanied by +/− icons and labels
- Keyboard: Tabs, menus, dialogs, grids fully keyboard accessible; focus trapping in modals
- ARIA: Landmark regions, aria-live for toasts, role=tablist with proper aria-selected
- Time: Show absolute timestamp with local timezone and ISO copy tooltip
- Localization-ready labels for states and event types
- Large tables: virtualized rows, sticky header, column resizing with handles and tooltips

Empty/loading/error states (examples)
- Loading: skeleton rows/cards; tab-level spinners only
- Empty impacts: “No impact data available yet” with “Refresh” and note about polling cadence
- Approval not permitted: inline alert “You’re not an eligible approver” with policy info tooltip
- Promotion failed: danger alert with retry guidance, link to Market Data promotion logs

Micro-frontend and platform integration
- Route namespace: all routes prefixed /scenarios to avoid collisions
- Share design tokens and base components with shell where possible
- External module deep-links expressed as shell-relative routes with query params
- Polling: central hook (aligned with “Micro-frontend Polling and UI Refresh” business logic)

Suggested UI entities for the architecture model (naming aligned to above)
- ui_screens
  - Scenarios Inbox (/scenarios/inbox): Triage scenarios and quick actions
  - Scenarios All (/scenarios/all): Explore/filter all scenarios
  - Scenario Details (/scenarios/:scenarioId): End-to-end review and actions
  - Scenario Details > Summary (/scenarios/:scenarioId/summary)
  - Scenario Details > Changes (/scenarios/:scenarioId/changes)
  - Scenario Details > Impacts (/scenarios/:scenarioId/impacts)
  - Scenario Details > Approvals (/scenarios/:scenarioId/approvals)
  - Scenario Details > Messages (/scenarios/:scenarioId/messages)
  - Scenario Details > Audit (/scenarios/:scenarioId/audit)
  - Audit Search (/scenarios/audit): Global audit trail
  - Admin > Policies (/scenarios/admin/policies)
  - Admin > Scenario Types (/scenarios/admin/types)
  - Admin > Reports (/scenarios/admin/reports)
- ui_components (selected)
  - ScenarioGrid, FiltersPanel, PageHeader, ContextBar, StatusBadge, ImpactDeltaChip, ParticipantsChips, ApprovalsProgress, ApprovalCTAs, AttestationModal, PromotionCTA, ConfirmationModal, MessagesThread, MessageComposer, AuditEventList, ReportTile, ExternalLinkButton, Toast, Skeleton, EmptyState
- ui_actions (selected)
  - Approve Scenario (trigger: button click; effect: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/approve)
  - Reject Scenario (trigger: button click; effect: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/reject)
  - Post Message (trigger: form submit; effect: POST /api/scenarios/{id}/messages)
  - Search Audit (trigger: search submit; effect: GET /api/audit)
  - Request Promotion (trigger: button click; effect: backend initiates promotion flow)

Open questions to finalize
- Filters/facets: Which attributes are must-have for Inbox and All (e.g., Desk/Book, Data Domain, Environment)?
- Impact headline: Which single metric should headline on cards and lists (e.g., worst delta by desk, aggregate VaR delta)?
- Approvals policy UX: Do you require ordered stages and SoD warnings, or simple parallel counts for MVP?
- Promotion targets: Single environment or multiple (UAT/Prod)? Any required fields in the Request Promotion modal?
- Messaging: Do we need @mentions and notifications now, or basic comments only for MVP?
- Deep links: Confirm the shell route patterns for Market Data, FRTB SA, and VaR so we can wire consistent ExternalLinkButtons.
- Admin: Are policy edits in scope for UI, or read-only with JSON preview for 2026?

If this structure looks right, I can prepare a concise list of ui_screens to upsert into the model (and optionally enumerate ui_actions), then we can move to component spec outlines (props, states, empty/loading/error) for top-priority screens.
I've just attached some low-fidelity wireframes for the 3 main screens, what are you opinions on these?

Thanks for sharing — here’s a quick, user-centered read of the wires and how I’d evolve them for the three main screens.

What I’m seeing
- A large circular dial/compass at the top (red ring, green ticks/needle) that reads like a portfolio “impact gauge.”
- Three loose zones beneath (left skinny area, a central strip, two larger oval shapes on the right) that feel like placeholders for navigation/list/cards or actions.

What’s working
- Strong visual focus for “at-a-glance” impact — good for a Summary view.
- Clear separation of page regions (headline metric vs. body content).
- Simplicity implies low cognitive load if we keep the content tight.

Main risks to address
- Space efficiency: The dial consumes prime vertical space. For enterprise users who triage via grids, it will push critical tables/actions below the fold.
- Ambiguity: Without labels, it’s hard to infer what the gauge shows (VaR delta? FRTB SA severity? Aggregate vs. the selected scenario).
- Color-only signaling: Red/green alone won’t meet accessibility. Pair with text, icons, and numeric deltas.
- Missing navigation and CTAs: I don’t yet see filters, tabs, or primary actions (Approve/Reject/Request Promotion), which are core to the flow.

Recommendations by screen

1) Scenario Inbox (triage)
- Replace the large dial with a compact header showing 2–3 KPI chips (e.g., “Awaiting approval: 7”, “High impact: 3”, “Exceptions: 12”).
- Add:
  - Top toolbar: Search, quick filters (My desk, Status, Type, Severity), date range.
  - Left filters panel (collapsible) for facets.
  - Main grid (sticky header): Name, Type, State, Headline impact delta, Exceptions, Approvals progress, Updated, Owner.
  - Optional right drawer: opens on row select for glance view and deep links (Market Data, FRTB SA, VaR).
- Primary action: Open Details. Secondary: Saved views, Refresh.

2) Scenario Details (end-to-end review)
- Keep a visual “impact overview,” but scale the dial to a card at the top-left of the Summary tab, not the page hero.
- Page frame:
  - Header: Title + ID, Type chip, State badge, headline impact delta chip, Updated.
  - Contextual CTAs (right side): Approve/Reject (if eligible), or Request Promotion once approvals met.
  - Tabs: Summary, Changes, Impacts, Approvals, Messages, Audit.
- Summary content:
  - Impact Overview (small dial or stacked mini-cards for FRTB SA/VaR with numeric deltas + trend).
  - Direct Changes card (count; deep link).
  - Approvals Progress (required vs. received; SoD indicators).
  - Recent Activity (5 latest events).
- Ensure accessibility: dial shows a number (e.g., “VaR Δ +3.2%”), color + icon (+/–), and a label.

3) Admin (policies/types/reports)
- Ditch the dial. Admin should be list/detail or form-centric.
- Left secondary nav: Policies, Scenario Types, Reports.
- Content area:
  - Policies table: name, required approver count, priority, enabled; row opens side drawer with JSON preview.
  - Scenario Types table: code, name, enabled, URL templates preview.
  - Reports table: key, version, last updated; sample data preview.

Interaction essentials to add to the next wire pass
- Approve/Reject flow: Attestation modal with policy-driven requirements (comment optional/required).
- Promotion request: Confirmation modal (target env if needed).
- Polling affordance: subtle “Updated just now” indicator; manual Refresh.
- Deep links: visible buttons for Market Data / FRTB SA / VaR that open within the shell.
- Empty/loading states: grid skeletons; “No impacts yet — try Refresh” in Impacts tab.

Visual and layout guidance
- 12-column grid; reserve the hero area for triage controls (Inbox) or header + CTAs (Details).
- Use cards for Summary metrics; keep tables primary on Inbox/Changes.
- Color: pair red/green with icons and text; ensure 4.5:1 text contrast.
- Keep heavy shapes (like the dial) ≤25% of the Summary tab width.

Questions to align the next iteration
- What single metric should headline the dial (if we keep it): aggregate VaR delta, worst-book delta, or policy-defined “impact severity”?
- On Inbox, which facets are must-have for day one (Desk/Book, Data domain, Environment, Status, Type)?
- Approvals: ordered stages and SoD enforcement in MVP, or parallel counts only?
- Promotion: single target environment for Q4’26, or choose (UAT/Prod) in the modal?

If you’d like, I can annotate your wireframes with these adjustments (regions, labels, component names) and produce a tightened v2 for each screen that maps directly to the routes and components we’ve defined.

What is the best way to display the impact in your opinion?  I want the transition from the governance screen to the impact screen to be an obvious change in mental mode?  How would be best handle the fact that there are multiple data sets i.e. all one screen and scrollable OR tabs areas OR accordion?

Short answer
- Display impacts as an “analysis canvas” with a clear visual shift from the governance list: large summary band + analytical visuals + focused filters.
- Use primary tabs for calculation families (FRTB SA, VaR) with deep links in the URL. Within each tab, use a sticky in‑page index (anchors) to jump to sections. Avoid one long scroll and avoid accordion-as-navigation.
- Offer an optional Compare toggle (side‑by‑side FRTB SA | VaR) on wide screens for power users.

Why this works
- It creates an obvious mental mode change: from triage (dense grid) to analysis (visual-first, fewer chrome elements).
- It matches your integrations: FRTB SA and VaR are distinct concepts and already link to separate external reports; top-level tabs reflect that mental model and support lazy loading.
- It remains accessible and efficient: tabs provide keyboardable, URL-addressable state; each section includes numeric tables alongside charts.

Detailed recommendation

1) Make the mode shift obvious (governance → analysis)
- Page frame: switch from table-first to visual-first.
  - Governance: dense grid, left facets.
  - Impacts: full-width summary band + charts; left collapsible Filters panel specific to the active calc; no right drawer by default.
- Visual cues:
  - “Analysis” badge near the header, different background tint (subtle) for the summary band, larger headline typography.
  - Persistent breadcrumb “Scenarios › [Name] › Impacts”.
  - Contextual deep links (Open full FRTB SA report, Open VaR report) visible up top.
- Controls move: hide bulk actions; keep only analysis filters and a Refresh.

2) Organize multiple datasets
- Primary top tabs (URL-driven): FRTB SA | VaR
  - Routes: /scenarios/:id/impacts?calc=frtb-sa and /scenarios/:id/impacts?calc=var
  - Lazy-load each tab; prefetch on hover/focus for perceived speed.
- Within a tab: sticky in-page index (left or top as pills) linking to sections:
  - Summary, Top Movers, Distribution, By Desk/Book, Exceptions, Generated Reports
  - Each section has a visible anchor (#top-movers etc.) for deep links from messages/audit.
- Accordions: use only inside a section for low-priority details (methodology notes, raw payloads). Don’t use accordions as the primary nav.

3) What to show in each tab (content hierarchy)
- Summary band (top)
  - KPI tiles: Headline Δ (absolute and %), Positions affected, Worst desk/book, Confidence/time horizon label
  - Two mini-cards: “Open full report” links for the calc with last-generated timestamp
- Key visuals (middle)
  - Waterfall: Top contributors to Δ (with numeric labels; color plus +/- icons)
  - Heatmap: Desk/Book contribution (sortable, clickable to filter)
  - Histogram/Distribution: if available, to show spread/volatility shift
  - All visuals paired with a “View as table” toggle or an adjacent compact grid
- Data tables (lower)
  - Top Movers table: risk factor/desk, baseline vs proposed, Δ, %Δ, link to detail
  - By Desk/Book table: totals and deltas with subtotal rows
- Generated Reports
  - List of ScenarioImpactReports with status and “Open” deep links into FRTB SA/VaR UIs
- Accessibility
  - Every chart shows the key number(s) inline; provide a data table view; no color-only encoding

4) Filters and interaction
- Filters panel (left, collapsible)
  - Common: date/run selector, desk/book, data domain, threshold (show |Δ| > x), show only increases/decreases
  - Calc-specific facets (e.g., FRTB SA risk class/bucket; VaR horizon/method)
  - “Apply” and “Reset” with chips under the header; keyboard-accessible
- Compare toggle (optional, desktop only)
  - Toggle to “Compare” shows FRTB SA and VaR side-by-side, mirroring the same sections
  - Route: /scenarios/:id/impacts/compare (or ?view=compare)
- Deep linking
  - Copy link preserves tab and anchor (e.g., …/impacts?calc=frtb-sa#top-movers) so teammates land on the same view
- Performance
  - Virtualize large tables; defer chart rendering until visible; skeletons for each section

5) What not to do
- One long scroll with everything: hard to orient, poor performance, no clear calc boundaries.
- Accordion-as-navigation: hides context, poor discoverability, clumsy with deep links.
- A giant hero gauge: space-inefficient for enterprise analysis; prefer multiple concise KPIs and task-focused charts.

Components to reuse
- ImpactTabs (top-level), InPageIndex (anchors), KPI Tile, WaterfallChart with Table, Heatmap with Table, Histogram with Table, FiltersPanel, ReportsList, ExternalLinkButton, EmptyState, Skeletons.

If you want, I can sketch a quick wire of the Impacts layout using this structure (header + tabs + anchors), and list the exact fields for the Top Movers and By Desk tables so your data contracts can align with the UI.
